heroLead: Cheat Lake reads as a recreational and residential community east of Morgantown, but the mineral rights under it often trace back to farmland that existed long before the reservoir did.
intro: The lake itself was formed by a dam built in the twentieth century, and the land around it was developed for housing and recreation well after that. Mineral rights under many Cheat Lake tracts were severed from the surface before any of that development, and it's common for a lakefront homeowner today to have no idea their property's mineral rights belong to someone else entirely, or the reverse: to hold a mineral interest under land they no longer live on.
We buy mineral and royalty interests around Cheat Lake directly, tracing the pre-development tract description through to the current record.

sections.heading: Reservoir development split old farm tracts
paragraphs: Damming the Cheat River and building out the surrounding community meant older agricultural tracts were reshaped, sold, and resurveyed. Mineral rights reserved before that process don't follow the new lot lines, so confirming your interest means going back to the original tract description.

sections.heading: A residential area with less obvious drilling activity
paragraphs: Cheat Lake doesn't have the visible well pad density of Marshall or Harrison County, but that doesn't mean the mineral rights are inactive. Monongalia County has ongoing Marcellus leasing, and pooled units can extend into this area from wells sited elsewhere.

sections.heading: Separating your surface property from your mineral interest
paragraphs: If you own a home at Cheat Lake and also hold a mineral interest, the two are legally distinct. We evaluate the mineral interest on its own terms, based on the underlying lease or unit status, not your property value.

faqs.question: I own a home at Cheat Lake. Do I automatically own the mineral rights under it?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. Many tracts here had mineral rights severed before development, so ownership of the surface and the minerals can belong to different people.

faqs.question: Is there active drilling near Cheat Lake?
faqs.answer: Visible surface drilling is limited in this residential area, but pooled units from nearby wells can still reach under Cheat Lake tracts. We check current unit status directly.

faqs.question: How do I find out if my family retained mineral rights when the land was developed?
faqs.answer: We trace the original tract's deed history through the Monongalia County record to confirm whether a mineral reservation was made and by whom.
